explain.say: A crystal is a solid whose atoms are stacked in a neat repeating pattern, like bricks in a wall. Salt, sugar, snowflakes and quartz are all crystals.

explain.say: Crystals grow from a liquid that holds more dissolved material than it can keep, because it is cooling or the water is evaporating. That extra material has to come out as solid.

explain.say: First a few particles lock together into a tiny seed. Then more particles join on, each fitting into the same pattern, so the crystal grows layer by layer with flat faces.

explain.say: The slower a crystal grows, the bigger and neater it gets, because particles have time to find their places. That is why crystals that grew slowly deep in the Earth can be huge.

faq.q: Why do crystals have flat faces?
faq.a: The atoms in a crystal fit together in a repeating pattern, like stacked boxes. As new layers add on, the pattern makes straight edges and flat faces with fixed angles between them.
asks: Why are crystals shaped like that?
Why do salt crystals look like cubes?

faq.a: A saturated solution holds as much dissolved material as it can at that temperature. If it cools or some water evaporates, the extra comes out as crystals.

faq.q: Why are some crystals big and others tiny?
faq.a: It depends on how fast they grow. Slow cooling or slow evaporation gives particles time to line up into big crystals; fast cooling makes many tiny ones.
asks: How do you grow a big crystal?

faq.q: How can I grow salt crystals at home?
faq.a: With an adult, stir salt into hot water until no more dissolves, pour it into a jar and hang a string in it. As the water cools and evaporates over days, salt crystals grow on the string.
They grow in cooling magma, in hot water flowing through cracks in rock, and where salty water evaporates. Huge crystals grow in caves where conditions stayed steady for a very long time.
asks: Where are crystals found in nature?

facts: Table salt, sodium chloride, forms cube-shaped crystals because of the way its ions stack.
Some gypsum crystals in the Cave of the Crystals in Mexico are over 10 metres long.

quiz.say: You want to grow the biggest crystals. What should you do?

options.show: Cool it as fast as possible
options.say: Cool it as fast as possible

quiz.why: Slow growth gives particles time to fit neatly into the pattern, making fewer, bigger crystals.

wrong.1: Fast cooling makes lots of tiny crystals.
wrong.2: Stirring disturbs growth and tends to make many small crystals.
